recentKeyChanges.title: Optimus production confirmed for late July/August 2026 at Fremont
recentKeyChanges.description: During Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings call, Elon Musk confirmed that Optimus humanoid robot production will commence in late July or August 2026 at the Fremont factory. The facility, converted from Model S/X production (final vehicles produced May 2026), targets 1 million units annually. Musk cautioned that initial output will be 'quite slow' due to 10,000 unique parts across an entirely new production line. Tesla is simultaneously constructing a second-generation Optimus facility at Giga Texas targeting 10 million units per year, with production starting summer 2027.

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla completes 46-day Model S/X line teardown for Optimus at Fremont
recentKeyChanges.description: Tesla Manufacturing posted a video on July 10, 2026 showing the original Model S and Model X assembly line at Fremont decommissioned in just 46 days — concrete pits, robotic arms, and conveyors removed. The post, captioned 'End of an era,' confirms the floor is being repurposed for Optimus. Limited Gen 3 production is already underway; full-scale output on the converted line remains targeted for late July or August 2026 with a long-term capacity ambition of 1 million units per year at Fremont.
